result.title: Scaling Laws of Ensemble Uncertainty in Language Models
result.summary: Many use cases for large language models (LLMs)---from AI safety to exploration and human interaction---can benefit from epistemic uncertainty estimates. We argue that existing Bayesian Deep Learning solutions, which are often restricted to a fixed model family, fail to capture the full epistemic uncertainty at practical LLM scales. This is because the error due to the bounded capacity of the model family remains invisible to disagreement among models supported by the prior. We relate this error to the well-known power-law scaling of LLM loss with model size. We then show that a second power law quantifies the shrinking disagreement within ensembles as model size increases. Its slower decay relative to the capacity law above suggests that ensembles capture a growing share of epistemic uncertainty and become more competitive as an axis for scaling, compared to a single larger model. Finally, a third power law quantifies the loss of ensemble diversity as members share a larger fraction of training before branching, and therefore identifies a further limitation, beyond the capacity error, for LoRA ensembles and optimization-based or second-order methods that approximate uncertainty around a single training solution. At a high level, these findings suggest diverse ensembles can be a promising axis, both for scaling and uncertainty quantification at larger scales.

AI.brief_summary: 该文讨论 LLM 的认知不确定性估计，指出受限于固定模型族的贝叶斯方法无法刻画容量误差，并给出三条幂律：损失随模型规模下降、集成内部分歧随规模下降（衰减更慢），以及成员共享训练比例增大导致集成多样性损失的规律。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「集成分歧作为不确定性信号」及共享训练导致多样性衰减的定量刻画，可供核查于 LVR 中多 latent 假设的多样性度量、基于不确定性的 STOP 决策与验证成本预测；但实验为纯文本规模律，向多模态视觉证据筛选的迁移尚待验证。
